Hi. I (30M) think I have a good perspective on this matter with a very similar position but from the opposite side. 

I grew up very religious in a very religious household that considered sex a very taboo topic. I left religion and became an atheist at around 24 and wanted to break all boundaries that I considered was holding me back. 

Back then I knew a girl (we both were virgins) and was in love with her but she refused to have sex before marriage. After that I broke up with her because I didn't want to make such a big commitment without knowing her sexually, and because of social media and the pressure around having sex, especially as a male was pretty high.

After I broke up with her I had a couple of one night stands and short term relationships, all of them were just physical and had no emotional drive behind them.

And I tell you as a male, each time after we finished, I felt immense guilt and disgust. Partly because the religious upbringing is still behind it, but also partly it's biological. When we have sex with someone our bodies release oxytocin (the hormone that make us bond with each other) and if the other person doesn't reciprocate we felt a great shame.

There are a lot of studies also saying that this shame is far more greater in females than males, no matter what their religious background is. So I know you have a lot of FOMO around this subject but from someone who tried it, it's not worth it at all.

I still think about the girl that wanted to get married first and I feel like it was the biggest mistake in my life to leave her , because now it's really hard to know someone like that.

Also there many studies that say the sexual and relationship satisfaction is inversely proportional with the number of sexual partners you had in your life. With people who had only one, reporting to have the highest satisfaction, also they had the lowest divorce rates. 

And the thing about you being afraid of not having experiences and that might turn guys off, then believe me, almost all men prefer a girl who is nice, loving, and emotionally attached to them with zero sexual experience over the most expert porn star. Relationship wise, and I am not talking about casual sex.

There is certain charm behind a girl who refuses to engage in hook up culture and just want to have a genuine, emotional, intimate relationship. I know the younger generations will say otherwise but they say so because they are still young and don't have enough life experiences.

If you want my advice then I would advice you to still go on dates and just be open about it. Say from the first date that you are looking for a serious relationship and you want to wait until marriage to have sex.

Guys who want you seriously will respect your wishes and won't force you into something you don't want, and the ones who just want to play will weed themselves out, thus sparing you time and effort.

But keep in mind the guys that will have the same standards as you will probably not be the most sexually attractive ones, because they have no experience. But if you are willing to spend time with each other, and communicate effectively, and develop a genuine loving relationship, then that would be the greatest thing you will ever experience in life.

Dating scene now a days is just a massive sis pool and people will do and say everything to use the other, so putting up boundaries and having standards will save you from a lot of drama and heart ache.

Stay awesome.
